top3.title: Socialist Night School: Abolition 101
top3.venue: Wooden Shoe
top3.why: Philly DSA's Socialist Night School turns to abolition this week, tracing the fight to defund police and prisons here back to global movements against racial capitalism and imperialism. It's political education in the true sense — an internationalist abolitionist framework, not just local talking points. Free, at Wooden Shoe, the city's anarchist bookstore and the most reliable venue in town for exactly this kind of programming.

top3.title: Special Event | Rare Finds: A Conversation With Collector Edward Leahy | In-Person
top3.venue: The Rosenbach Museum and Library, 2008-2010 Delancey St
top3.why: Collector Edward Leahy opens up eight centuries of literary history for one intimate evening at the Rosenbach — illuminated manuscripts, jeweled bindings, incunabula, and what's likely the world's finest private Beatrix Potter collection, alongside first editions of horror classics. A rare chance to hear a serious collector talk through how and why he built this, not just look at it behind glass.

top3.title: Mike D 5D
top3.venue: Union Transfer, 1026 Spring Garden St., Philadelphia, PA 19123
top3.why: Mike Diamond — Mike D of the Beastie Boys — brings his “5D” tour to Union Transfer, a rare non-NYC stop from a founding figure of New York hip-hop who discovered punk rock as a teenager and never fully let go of it. Expect stories as much as a set: this reads as a conversational, career-spanning night rather than a straight concert. Spring Garden, a few blocks from the Broad Street Line's Spring Garden stop.

top3.title: The Damned
top3.venue: Union Transfer, 1026 Spring Garden St., Philadelphia, PA 19123
top3.why: The Damned — one of the bands that invented UK punk in the first place — play Union Transfer on the kind of night Philly's punk and goth lineages both claim as their own. Decades in, they're still theatrical, still gothic, still genuinely dangerous live. Support from Flamin' Groovies and The Courettes rounds out a stacked bill.

top3.title: TROLL 2 w/ actor George Hardy in attendance!
top3.venue: PhilaMOCA, 531 N. 12th St, Philadelphia, PA 19123
top3.why: George Hardy — the dentist-turned-accidental-icon of “Best Worst Movie” fame — returns to PhilaMOCA in person for a Halloween-season screening of TROLL 2, the gloriously inept 1990 cult object that's outlived every movie that was actually trying to be good. Expect a full post-screening Q&A, not just a film on a loop. $24.20.

Free, South Street.

top3.title: Osees ft. Brigid Dawson
top3.venue: Union Transfer, 1026 Spring Garden St., Philadelphia, PA 19123
top3.why: Osees — the long-running, shape-shifting garage-punk project led by John Dwyer — bring their new record ABOMINATION REVEALED AT LAST. to Union Transfer, an album Dwyer describes as a direct, pummeling reaction to the current moment's stack of catastrophes. Loud, political, and uncompromising in exactly the way their decades-long catalog has trained you to expect.

top3.title: THESE PEOPLE w/ filmmaker Cory McAbee in attendance

It's an assembled, genre-scrambling film about Lincoln's assassination, narrated by an immortal who was in the room, which is about as deep a cut as repertory programming gets here. $14.52.
